title: Granuloma as a histopathology class
dek: Wikipedia's granuloma page is broader than TB: foreign-body versus immune, giant cells, sarcoid look-alikes. TB architecture stays on tb-granuloma.
story: Granuloma on Wikipedia (Q1129338) is a tissue pattern: macrophages organised, often with giant cells, in response to something hard to clear. TB is the celebrity example, not the only one (sarcoid, foreign body, fungi, Crohn in some telling).

Langhans-type giant cells and caseation push the prior toward mycobacteria/fungi, still not a species. Simplfy's tb-granuloma plate is the TB lesion with oxygen and drug gradients. This card is the dictionary class those lesions belong to.
TNF and IFN-γ appear on the encyclopedia page as organisers of immune granulomas. That is a pointer to host plates, not a biologic licence.
deep: Foreign-body granulomas lack the same T-cell programme. Do not paste TB immunology onto a suture granuloma.
Necrotising versus non-necrotising is a useful split; sarcoid is classically non-necrotising, TB often necrotising — with exceptions that wreck slogans.
Anti-TNF dissolving granulomas is why reactivation TB is a clinic problem (tb-tnf-cd4).
Do not diagnose from a Wikipedia image board.
